identity.real_world_identity_notes: Reiza's renamed Ferrari 550 Maranello: the GT1 car Prodrive built for Care Racing Development, which raced the FIA GT Championship from 2001 to 2005 and Le Mans through 2006. AMS2 carries it as Milano 55 GT1. The record previously treated the renaming as a fictional car and declined to name an analogue; the maintainer identified it. A six-speed Xtrac sequential and a 600 bhp V12 agree with the six sequential gears and the automatic cut found in the drive, the cut being the car's flat-shift facility worked by an optical sensor at the base of the gearlever.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a round rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
All six sequential-stick gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts with automatic throttle cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted and no automatic throttle blip was observed; authentic rev matching therefore requires the driver to blip the throttle manually.
The Ferrari 575 GTC resemblance remains unconfirmed and is not used as an identity match.

The real car needs the clutch for every downshift and does not need it for an upshift when flat-shifting. AMS2 accepts a clutchless downshift, which is recorded as a simulator override so both layers stay true: the authentic technique is to use the clutch on the way down.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Standing-start clutch, six-speed sequential stick without paddles, automatic cut, no automatic blip, and round no-display rim were directly observed.

overrides.condition: AMS2 accepts a downshift with no clutch input, where the real car requires it.

confidence.basis: Observed directly in the guided drive: the downshift was accepted with no clutch input, while the registered technical account says the real car requires the clutch for every downshift.

Exact simulator identity, cockpit controls, and shift behavior were directly tested. Ferrari sources are retained only as clearly qualified period context and do not establish the fictional car's identity.

notes: Observed live in AC 14923034 via guided verification observation ac.gt-ferruccio-55-v12.20260822t200835844z-3f8b6f4d by Jason Kinslow.

overrides.condition: The fingerprinted RSS v4 implementation accepted the tested coast downshift without physical clutch input, where the real Prodrive car requires the clutch for every downshift.

confidence.basis: The guided coast-downshift test directly observed acceptance without driver clutch input.

overrides.condition: The fingerprinted RSS v4 implementation accepted the tested coast downshift without driver throttle input and produced no automatic blip, while the curated real-car technique requires the driver to rev-match.

confidence.basis: The guided drive directly observed coast-downshift acceptance with no driver blip and detected no automatic throttle spike.

The fingerprinted RSS Ferruccio 55 package is an Italian V12 early-2000s GT and bundles Prodrive, Care, BMS, JMB, Larbre, and Russian Age liveries corresponding to the 550 GTS Maranello. The registered technical account independently establishes the real Prodrive car's six-speed sequential transmission and shift technique. The AC behavior and cockpit were directly observed.

claims.basis: Official release context and exact live Milano GT55 / GT1_05 observation establish the simulated identity without asserting a real-world analogue.
The sources document period hardware and the fictional Reiza name but do not establish a Ferrari mapping; the record explicitly preserves that limitation.
Direct current-game testing and cockpit inspection establish the modeled hardware, start clutch, automatic cut, absence of automatic blip, required manual rev matching, and wheel shape.

The registered technical account gives a six-speed Xtrac sequential with a flat-shift facility, needing no clutch for an upshift and the clutch for every downshift, which the drive's six gears and automatic cut agree with. It says nothing about the rim or about what the simulator does, so those stay on the drive.

RSS v6 identifies the exact Ferruccio 55 implementation; its installed v4 metadata and bundled team, year, and livery labels converge on the Prodrive Ferrari 550 GTS Maranello already curated as Milano 55 GT1. This review maps the mod implementation to that real-car record without treating the fictional telemetry name as the car's identity.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

deviations.basis: The Prodrive-built Xtrac sequential takes the clutch on every downshift, where the archetype's cars need it only to pull away. This is the only curated record that needs the clutch for a shift already under way. AMS2 accepts a clutchless downshift, which is carried as a simulator override rather than changing the real car.
